notes.title: Update — Windows 11 Compatibility
notes.notes:
[h2]Windows 11 Compatibility Bug Fix — March 2025[/h2]
[h3]From HeR Interactive[/h3]

What changed:

The latest update fixes a common 'flickering screen' problem on newer Windows 11 computers.
We have seen your comments and workarounds on the message boards and worked to resolve this issue for everyone.

We're so happy that these games continue to bring joy on hardware so far ahead of the time these stories were written!

[h3][b]Potential bug:[/b][/h3]
In some cases, drivers have been out of date. We recommend updating your drivers. You can find instructions for doing so here: [url=https://www.herinteractive.com/2014/04/graphics-problems/]https://www.herinteractive.com/2014/04/graphics-problems/[/url]

If this doesn't help, we suggest deleting the [u][b]d3d9.dll[/b][/u] file from the game folder, then launching the game again. You can find the game folder by clicking the gear icon on the game's page in your steam library and selecting [b]manage > browse local files[/b]. This will put you in a position previous to this update. We apologize for any inconvenience the update may have caused.

[img]https://www.herinteractive.com/wp-content/uploads/Steam-Announcement-Image-2025-Mar.png[/img]

Happy sleuthing!

notes.title: Kat Brewster s 5 best games of 2018
notes.notes:
We asked a bunch of our regular writers to tell us what their five favourite games this year were. Today it’s the turn of Priceless Play‘s curator Kat Brewster.

One of these games is a board game, one of them is a Nintendo game, and most of them didn’t come out this year. We are allowing this because it is very on brand for Kat.

I wracked my brain over the past few weeks, trying to think of games I played in 2018. This seems to happen every year around GOTY time much like when someone asks you what your favourite movie is, and you forget whether you ve actually ever seen a movie. Did Did I play any video games? Did any games even come out? Surely there must have been at least one.

In the precious little free time I scraped together during term (like coins from sofa cushions to get a snack from the office vending machine), I managed to discover (or re-discover) a handful of games this year. They re a bit covered in lint, but I promise they re still good.
